description: Eight children are said to be among those killed by the strike, which hit a gathering of displaced people.

description: The US embassy says it is "aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport", which come days after Yemen's Houthis said they had struck it.

description: Ukraine's leader had said the deal with Russia to release diesel into the US would help Moscow fund the war.

description: Navi Pillay, who won this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, fought racism in South Africa, shaping her international career as a judge and advocate for justice and human rights.

title: UK government blocks Northern Ireland march after standoff fueled sectarian tensions
description: LONDON: The British government has blocked a contentious march from taking place in Northern Ireland after a two-week standoff between groups that support the region’s continued union with the United Kingdom and those who favor reunification with the Republic of Ireland. title: Germany pursues new Russia sanctions despite US diesel deal
description: Germany remains committed to pursuing new EU sanctions against Russia despite Moscow reaching a diesel release deal with the US, emphasizing its steadfast support for Ukraine.

title: Omani FM condemns attacks on Saudi airports in phone call with Prince Faisal
description: RIYADH: Oman’s foreign minister on Saturday condemned the recent Houthi attacks on two Saudi international airports and reaffirmed solidarity with the Kingdom during a phone call with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan. description: Matt Renshaw’s unbeaten century led Australia’s fightback against South Africa on the second day of the first test in Durban.

title: Trump rages over Nobel Peace Prize loss
description: President Trump lashed out late Friday night after he once again did not win the Nobel Peace Prize he has openly coveted. Why it matters: The award is Trump's white whale, an honor he talks about frequently and believes he deserves. title: India's 'cockroach' movement: "This is unprecedented"
description:
Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, head of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, on Saturday ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission, the party said.

"This is unprecedented," our guest Subir Sinha, director of the SOAS South Asia Institute, says.

title: Trump hails Russia deal to release diesel as midterms loom
description: US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had secured Russia's agreement for a major release of diesel, as he eased war sanctions on Moscow in a push to lower energy costs ahead of midterm elections.

title: Live: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 15 in Zaporizhzhia, cause power outages in Kyiv
description: Russian strikes on the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed at least 15 people, including three children, regional authorities said on Saturday. The attack also caused "large-scale power outages" in the capital Kyiv and the surrounding region. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

title: Lens see off Lyon as Ligue 1 season resumes after international break
description: Lens put an end to a four-match winless run by beating Lyon 2-1 on Friday night, in what was the first Ligue 1 fixture after a three-week international break. Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique has brushed off concerns about Ousmane Dembélé's recent form, having rested the forward for Saturday's match against promoted side Le Mans.

title: Yemen says advancing against Houthis around key Bab al-Mandab strait
description: Yemen said Saturday that forces were advancing against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait. This comes a week after the country's Saudi-backed government announced that it was initiating a counter-offensive to take back territory seized by the pro-Iran group during last month's lightning offensive.

title: October 7 scars push Israel's first-time voters to right
description: Like hundreds of thousands of Israelis, Amihai will be of voting age for the first time since Hamas carried out its attack on October 7, 2023. When he casts his ballot this month, he has one priority above all -- security.

title: Hunger and malnutrition stalk Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
description: Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family. It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.
